_nota: Contraparte en inglés de measurement_cost.json (2026-11-15): cada cadena castellana que se enseña (`equipment`, `crew_time_basis`, `inputs_basis`, el `basis` de cada regla, el `where` y la `note` de lo leído y el `searched` de lo buscado) con su inglés. Las claves son el castellano exacto; los identificadores de regla, las fichas, las fechas y las frases copiadas de una fuente (`quote`) no se traducen, y lo que se escribe igual en los dos idiomas no está. Las clases siguen siendo relativas y sin medir: el inglés no afirma más que el castellano. Lo aplica `ingest/cost.py` (`_served`) al servir. Traducción automática, sin revisar por una persona; lo vigila tests/test_cost_en.py.

strings.No hereda de su entrada. En EMMA esta do: It does not inherit from its input. In EMMA this dose is not calculated: it arrives recorded from outside (`POST /api/observations`, from a dosimeter) and the risk engine reads the latest one. The absorbed dose rate is one of its inputs, not the only one: the effective dose that NASA-STD-3001 [V1 4030] asks for is calculated with the NASA Q model, which needs the particle spectrum, and no source of EMMA publishes it (`environment/dosimetry.py`). What EMMA does calculate on board from the recorded rate is the dose of this mission (`analysis/radiation.py`, `mission_dose`), inferred with a mean quality factor, and it is not this indicator. Where the cumulative dose that arrives is calculated was searched for on 2026-10-22 (`searched_not_found`): on the ISS there is one dosimeter that is read on return and another that gives it on board, and EMMA does not say which one it arrives from; it remains unclassified.
strings.Sale del mismo informe de laboratorio qu: It comes from the same laboratory report as its analytes: the Polaris extractor reads it from the lab report together with the neutrophils and the lymphocytes (`reports/labs.py`, `LAB_KEYS`: `nlr`). Where there is no report there is no ratio: it is processed where they are processed and arrives when they arrive.
strings.Polaris lo deriva de la urea y la creati: Polaris derives it from the urea and the creatinine of the same report (`reports/labs.py`, `LAB_KEYS`: `bun_cr`, urea / 2.14 ÷ creatinine): there is no ratio without those two analytes, and it is processed and arrives as they do.

strings.En la ISS, la camiseta y la cinta con se: On the ISS, the CSA shirt and band with sensors (pulse and ECG, blood pressure, breathing, skin temperature, saturation and activity) do not give their analysis on board: the battery plugs into a base that downlinks the data to Earth. EMMA's wearables give the value on the device itself; the sentence says that on the station equipment the scientific analysis is done on Earth. It does not say whether the crew member sees any value on board. It qualifies only the sensors that are worn (pulse, variability, breathing, saturation, temperature, sleep, impacts): the rule also reaches the ship dosimeter and the exercise equipment log, and the sentence does not speak of them.
strings.Solo sobre el tiempo hasta la postura es: Only about the time to a stable posture (standing up after lying down, and sit-to-stand): the time is calculated from the inertial sensor data with a threshold. The sentence does not say whether that calculation is done on the sensor itself at the time or afterwards, on a computer: it qualifies the rule without contradicting it.
strings.Solo sobre las ecografías: en la ISS el: Only about the ultrasound scans: on the ISS the ultrasound scanner plugs into the HRF rack, which powers it and downlinks the probe video to Earth in real time. The rule says the value comes from the instrument; the sentence says the image also reaches Earth while it is being taken. It does not say where the value is measured.
strings.Solo sobre la ecografía de la yugular in: Only about the internal jugular ultrasound of that study (the left one): the acquisition on the station was guided in real time by researchers on Earth. It is a dependence on Earth when taking the measurement, not when analyzing it: the rule does not capture it, and it is noted as operator training and guidance in the rule `ecografia-yugular-guiada-desde-tierra`.
strings.Solo sobre el área de la yugular interna: Only about the area of the left internal jugular in that study: the device did not give it on measuring; two independent sonographers outlined it by hand afterwards. The sentence does not say where or when, but it is neither “on the device itself” nor “immediate”: it qualifies both classes of the rule for that measurement. In EMMA the area is measured in the ultrasound console (`imaging/`), and the rule describes that.
strings.Una demostración tecnológica (diciembre: A technology demonstration (December 2020 and January 2021) counted leukocytes with a five-part differential on board, in capillary blood of one crew member, in the third session. It is a demonstration, not equipment in ordinary use; its microcuvettes are discarded after each use (slide 4).
strings.La misma demostración, contada por otro: The same demonstration, told by another NASA document two years later.
strings.Un recuento de glóbulos rojos hecho a bo: A red blood cell count done on board in one session of a study (Venous Flow). The entry does not name the equipment or say that it is in ordinary use.
strings.Divulgación: dice que hay equipo portáti: Outreach: it says there is portable equipment that analyzes blood on board, without naming the equipment or the analytes. The same entry tells that the blood and urine of the CIPHER study were frozen «for preservation and later analysis».
strings.Otra demostración tecnológica de analiza: Another technology demonstration of an on-board blood analyzer; the abstract does not say which analytes or that it stayed in use.
strings.Un equipo diseñado para medir a bordo y: Equipment designed to measure on board and in real time the volume of each void. In February 2009 it had not yet flown to the ISS.
strings.El UMS llegó a la ISS en 2011. Lo leído: The UMS reached the ISS in 2011. What was read does not say whether it was then used routinely or whether it replaced the lithium bags: the paper gives it as a plan. Searched on 2026-10-21 and not found: in NTRS («Urine Monitoring System»: nine records, none published after 2011; «Broyan urine»: what comes after 2011 deals with the urine processor, not the UMS), in the text of two later ICES papers on the ISS toilet (ICES-2019-154, which only names the UMS wash-water inlet on the toilet panel; ICES-2021-035, which does not name it) and on the NASA website (the old record of the UMS experiment on nasa.gov answers 404, and the search returned no station daily report that names it). Nor does the 2017 study that used the lithium bags say in which years its crew members flew. Searched again on 2026-10-22 and not found: on the web, for the UMS in the station daily reports from 2012 to 2015 and in the station blog (no entry names it), and for its commissioning, removal or nominal use in Node 3 (only the development papers from 2009 to 2011 come up, and those of the later toilet, the Universal Waste Management System, which do not say what became of the UMS). Nor is it listed in the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project), whose urine consumables are the collection device, the containment bag, the syringes and a pH kit, without naming the UMS.
strings.En el protocolo de medidas estándar de N: In the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025, the 24 h urine —and with it its volume— is collected only before and after the flight, on Earth. It does not contradict “on Earth”: it says that in that protocol the datum does not exist during the mission.
strings.Con el UMS la micción no va a una bolsa: With the UMS the void does not go into a lithium bag: the equipment measures the volume and allows the sample to be taken by syringe («allow for syringe sampling», abstract of the same paper), which is also used up. What was read does not say whether it later replaced the bags (searched on 2026-10-21 without finding it: see the same discrepancy in `orina-24h-en-tierra`).
strings.En el protocolo de medidas estándar de N: In the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 no urine is collected in flight: what is used up is the collection on Earth before and after the flight («A 24-hour, void-by-void urine collection is completed using 500-mL bottles»), not on-board material.

In the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025, the EDTA tube is taken before and after the flight, on Earth. The next sentence of the article says that in flight only two serum tubes are collected («During flight, 15 mL blood is collected in two 7.5 mL SSTs»): in that protocol there is no EDTA tube on board.
strings.La frase que sigue nombra entre esos aná: The sentence that follows names among those analyses the complete blood count, with the count of leukocytes, neutrophils and lymphocytes («These tests include complete blood count»). The flight samples of that protocol are frozen until return: the blood count does not come from them. The 2015 study, by contrast, returned the flight blood to Earth in under 48 h to analyze it at once («returned to Earth within 48 h of collection for immediate analysis»).
strings.En el protocolo de medidas estándar de N: In the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025, the EDTA tube —and with it the complete blood count— is taken before and after the flight, on Earth; in flight only two serum tubes are collected. The 2017 study is earlier and took the EDTA tube in flight as well.
strings.No cambia lo que gasta —el tubo es el mi: It does not change what is used up —the tube is the same— but it qualifies what arrives: the flight blood waited up to 48 h at ambient temperature before analysis, and in that time the hematocrit, the MCV and the MCHC did not stay stable in the stability test of the same study. Coming from the same tube does not make them equally reliable.
strings.Un concepto de operaciones para Marte, n: A concept of operations for Mars, not what exists today: it assumes a urine dipstick for calcium oxalate on board. It is not the 24-hour collection or the laboratory profile, and it gives no unit: it does not change where EMMA's eight analytes are processed, but it says that for a distant mission an on-board measurement is being considered.
strings.En el protocolo de medidas estándar de N: In the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 the 24 h urine is collected only before and after the flight: in that protocol, the possible frequency in flight is none. The rule follows the protocol that did take it in flight, and says so.
strings.En el estudio de los virus latentes el p: In the latent virus study the 24 h urine pool was also collected only before and after the flight; in flight there was a single urine sample per crew member («There was only one urine sample inflight», note to table 3). Two protocols, two cadences: the rule does not invent EMMA's.
strings.Ese experimento de nutrición tomó orina: That nutrition experiment took urine in flight; the sentence does not say which analytes were measured in it, and so it is not read as this profile. Two protocols, two cadences.
strings.El hemograma no aguanta la congelación y: The blood count does not withstand freezing, and blood at ambient temperature rarely comes back from space: what the rule describes is what that study did, not what is ordinarily done with flight blood, which is frozen (`suero-congelado-a-bordo`).
strings.En el protocolo de medidas estándar de N: In the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 the saliva for virology is stored frozen; the sentence does not say whether on board or already on Earth. Two protocols, two destinations: the rule follows the study that says where the sample waited and shows the other beside it.
strings.Clase «continuo y pasivo» de este ficher: Class “continuous and passive” of this file (`mode`): the sensor gives it while it is worn or running, with no sample to take to an analyzer and no analysis to wait for. Qualification read on 2026-10-22, only about the sensors that are worn: on the ISS, the CSA shirt with sensors (Bio-Monitor) downlinks its data to Earth for the scientific analysis (see discrepancies).
strings.Clase «periódico, no invasivo» de este f: Class “periodic, non-invasive” of this file (`mode`), which `ingest/cost.py` sets against “periodic, with a sample”: with no sample there is no analyzer and no analysis to wait for; the value comes from the instrument or from the note. Qualification read on 2026-10-23, only about the ultrasound scans: on the ISS the probe video is downlinked to Earth in real time, the jugular acquisition was guided from Earth and its area was outlined afterwards by two sonographers (see discrepancies). Qualification read on 2026-10-31, only about the two sensorimotor tests of Standard Measures: the percentage of correct steps of the tandem walk is counted afterwards by three reviewers on the video, and the time to a stable posture is given by the inertial sensor data (see discrepancies).
strings.Clase «calculado a partir de otras medid: Class “calculated from other measurements” of this file (`mode`): it is a calculation; it takes no sample and uses no material of its own. Where it is processed and when it arrives depend on its inputs, which each calculated indicator names in `inputs` (since 2026-10-21) and from which it inherits if `inherits` says so.
strings.`equipment` de este fichero: el valor es: `equipment` of this file: the value is what the crew member notes down in the console (`api/diary.py` for self-report, diary and intake record; `api/pain.py` for the pain map), with no sample and no material.
strings.`equipment` de este fichero y el código: `equipment` of this file and the code that scores it: the PVT is a reaction time test —a stimulus on screen and a key— and what is recorded are the reaction times in milliseconds (`ingest/pvt.py`, `score`), with no sample and no material. In EMMA it is run by the crew console (`frontend/src/pvt/PvtPanel.tsx`, `POST /api/pvt/console`); the one that arrives from other equipment through `POST /api/pvt` is the same list of times. What the test costs in crew time does have a source (`crew_time_basis`); of the screen on which it is run on board, no source read says that it uses anything up, and this rule does not claim it of the screen: it says the test uses no material of its own.
strings.Leído en NASA: en la ISS medir el recuen: Read at NASA: on the ISS measuring the leukocyte count is “an unmet need” (Perusek et al., 2022), and in the six-month immune study the blood samples were taken in flight and returned for analysis, with the leukocyte distribution among what was measured (Crucian et al., 2010); its full publication says they returned to Earth in under 48 h and that the count was done with a clinical hematology analyzer (Crucian et al., 2015). The deferred result follows from that. Qualification: a technology demonstration did make a count with a leukocyte differential on board (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído: «hoy» la sangre tomada en la ISS: Read: “today” the blood taken on the ISS is frozen and returned to be analyzed after the mission (Brawley et al., 2025), and the ISS nutrition experiment took blood and urine in flight to analyze them after return (Smith et al., 2012). The sentences speak of the sample, not of each analyte: they name blood, not sodium or CA-125. The deferred result follows from that. Qualification: there are demonstrations and one study session that analyzed blood on board (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído: el experimento de nutrición de la: Read: the ISS nutrition experiment took blood and urine in flight to analyze them after the return to Earth (Smith et al., 2012). The sentence speaks of the urine sample, not of the marker. The 24 h collection and the specific gravity with dipstick or refractometer are not included: their equipment is different and the sentence does not say where they are measured. The 24 h volume has its own rule, read since 2026-10-20 (`orina-24h-en-tierra`); the specific gravity still has no source.
strings.Leído en NASA: en la ISS la saliva se re: Read at NASA: on the ISS saliva is collected routinely for stress hormones and latent virus DNA, and research on the ISS usually stores the samples and returns them to Earth for analysis (Gutierrez et al., 2026); in the six-month immune study, the saliva taken in flight was returned for analysis (Crucian et al., 2010). The deferred result follows from that.
strings.Leído: en los estudios de la ISS el volu: Read: in the ISS studies the volume of the urine taken in flight is not measured on board. Each void is collected in a bag with a known amount of tracer (lithium), a sample is taken by syringe and, after landing, the lithium is analyzed to calculate the volume of each void and prepare the 24 h pools (Broyan and Cibuzar, 2009; Mehta et al., 2017). The deferred result follows from that: the sample waits frozen for the return. Qualification: equipment designed to measure the volume on board (UMS) was launched to the ISS in 2011, and in the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 there is no urine collection in flight (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído: en vuelo, la orina se recoge en b: Read: in flight, urine is collected in bags (Urine Collection Devices) that carry a known amount of tracer —1 mL of lithium chloride solution per void— and is sampled by syringe (Broyan and Cibuzar, 2009; Mehta et al., 2017; Rodriguez and Broyan, 2011); the bags weigh in what has to be sent up to the station and in the trash that has to be stored (Feeback et al., 2009). The sentences speak of every urine sample taken in flight («medical urine samples»), not of the marker: they reach the 24 h volume and the NTX, which is measured in laboratory urine, although none comes from the study that measured the NTX. The specific gravity with dipstick or refractometer is not included: no sentence read says how it is measured. Qualification: the equipment that would measure the volume on board (UMS) and the current protocol with no urine in flight (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído: con un glucómetro, la gota de san: Read: with a glucose meter, the drop of blood from the finger goes onto a strip that is inserted into the device itself, and the reading appears after a few seconds, with no separate analysis to wait for (CDC, «Monitoring Your Blood Sugar»); the lancet and the strip are thrown away after each measurement, and the strips are damaged by moisture or heat and are kept closed: they are used up. The sentences are from Earth and for people with diabetes; they say nothing about flight, and whether there is a glucose meter on board the ISS no source read says.
strings.Leído: en vuelo, la sangre para la bioqu: Read: in flight, the blood for the biochemistry of the NASA standard measures protocol is collected in two 7.5 mL serum separator tubes (SST), and the samples are stored in the ISS freezer until they return to Earth (Hardy et al., 2025): the tube is used up with the sample. The sentence speaks of the blood draw, not of each analyte: it names the serum, not sodium or CA-125, and it reaches the analytes that EMMA measures in serum. The blood count (leukocytes and their differential, red cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, indices and platelets) is not included: it is measured in whole blood, not in the serum of those tubes. Its tube in flight has rules of its own, read in the studies that measured it (`hemograma-leucocitos-en-tubo-edta` and, since 2026-10-22, `hemograma-serie-roja-en-tubo-edta`).
strings.Leído: en el estudio inmunitario de NASA: Read: in the NASA immune study with 23 ISS crew members, each blood sample —the three taken in flight too— was one tube with ACD and another with EDTA, and the leukocyte count was verified in the EDTA one because ACD dilutes the sample (Crucian et al., 2015): the tube is used up with the sample. The sentence speaks of the sample of that study, which measured the leukocyte count and its distribution: it reaches the leukocytes and their differential, absolute and in percent. The red cell series, the indices and the platelets are not included: that study did not measure them (another rule read since 2026-10-22 reaches them, `hemograma-serie-roja-en-tubo-edta`). Qualification: in the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025, the blood count goes in an EDTA tube only before and after the flight, because it cannot be measured in a frozen sample (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído: en el estudio de NASA sobre el he: Read: in the NASA study on the blood count of 31 ISS crew members, the blood —also that taken in flight, at the start, in the middle and at the end of the mission— was collected in a 10 mL EDTA tube and returned to Earth at ambient temperature for analysis (Kunz et al., 2017): the tube is used up with the sample. The analyzers measure the red cell count, the MCV, the hemoglobin and the platelets, and calculate the rest of the indices from them: the sentence reaches the red cell series, its indices (hematocrit, MCH, MCHC) and the platelets, which come from the same tube. Qualifications: in the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025, the EDTA tube of the blood count is taken only before and after the flight; and in the same 2017 study, after the 48 h wait, the hematocrit, the MCV and the MCHC did not stay stable (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído: en el inventario del equipo médic: Read: in the inventory of the ISS medical research equipment published by NASA (ISS Medical Project, revised in June 2016), the ultrasound gel («Echo Gel») is listed among the consumables of the green HRF supply kit, and the ultrasound scanner of that inventory is the Ultrasound 2, which is kept in a drawer of HRF-1: the scan uses up gel. What was read does not say how much gel each scan uses, nor does it tie the gel to a piece of equipment by name: «echo» is ultrasound, and the Ultrasound 2 is the only ultrasound scanner in the inventory. It reaches all of EMMA's measurements made with an ultrasound scanner (optic nerve sheath, internal jugular and bladder): what is used up is the coupling of the probe, not the site scanned. It is a 2016 inventory: it does not say which scanner or which gel is on board today.
strings.Leído: en el estudio de NASA sobre virus: Read: in the NASA study on latent viruses in long ISS missions, the saliva for diurnal cortisol was collected on filter paper, which was left to air-dry and stored until return (Mehta et al., 2017): the paper is used up with the sample.
strings.Leído: en el mismo estudio, la saliva pa: Read: in the same study, the saliva to look for viruses was collected with cotton rolls (Salivette), which were stored in a bag with stabilizing buffer (Mehta et al., 2017): the roll and the bag are used up with the sample.
strings.Los dos cocientes se calculan de los ana: The two ratios are calculated from the analytes of the same report (`reports/labs.py`, `nlr` and `bun_cr`; their `inputs` in this file): they add no equipment, instrument or operator of their own. The mass, the power, the calibration and the training of the analyzer of their inputs are not inherited, and in them they remain unclassified. The cumulative dose, also of class “calculated”, is left out: in EMMA it arrives recorded; it is not calculated (its `inputs_basis`).
strings.Leído en el informe diario de la estació: Read in the station daily report of 29 October 2019 (NASA): after moving the SLAMMD mass measurement device to another rack, the crew mounted the calibration arm, put the calibration mass on it and made a control measurement. The sentence says the device is calibrated; it does not say how often or whether it is done before each weighing (that one was the check after the move). The other on-board mass measurement device, the Russian one (BMMD), was not read.
strings.Leído en el resumen de las instalaciones: Read in the summary of the ISS human research facilities (NASA HRP, revised in June 2023): the HRF gas system supplies, in cylinders, breathing and calibration mixtures for ESA's portable pulmonary function analyzer (PPFS) and for the periodic fitness tests of medical operations on the cycle ergometer (Max CEVIS), and it names the calibration mixture of the PPFS. It is the gas analyzer of the station's exercise test, the same one whose material was searched for in the fifteenth round. It does not say how often it is calibrated. Whether the calibration gas counts as a consumable of the measurement is not decided here: the consumables of the test remain unclassified.
strings.Leído en el estudio de la yugular intern: Read in the study of the internal jugular in eleven ISS crew members (Marshall-Goebel et al., 2019): everything taken on the station was guided in real time from Earth. Only the left one: the study did not take the right one («only the left IJV was imaged»), and for the optic nerve sheath and the bladder it was not read who guides the acquisition. It does not say what prior training the person holding the probe had. Guiding from Earth is a dependence on Earth: it is noted here, without deducing what would happen with the light time of another mission.
strings.Leído de los dos dosímetros de zona de l: Read about the two ISS area dosimeters that were searched for: the silicon detectors of the DOSTELs of the DOSIS 3D experiment, in the Columbus laboratory, were thoroughly calibrated before launch with several radiation sources (Berger et al., 2017), and to NASA's REMs, spread over six station modules, calibrations are applied to convert what is measured into deposited energy (SRAG page, updated on 24 September 2025). EMMA does not say which is its “ship dosimeter”, the one for each crew member's rate: the environment series it reads by default is that of DosTel in OSDR RadLab (`environment/radlab.py`), against which the simulator's rate was compared (`ingest/simulator.py`), and the recorded rate arrives from an unnamed dosimeter. That is why the rule cites the two area dosimeters read and does not choose one: both say they are calibrated; they do not say how often, or whether recalibration is done on board, or who does it. The cumulative dose is not included: it arrives recorded from a dosimeter that EMMA does not name (`searched_not_found`).
strings.Leído en el estudio de NASA sobre el hem: Read in the NASA study on the blood count of 31 ISS crew members (Kunz et al., 2017), the same one that gives the EDTA tube of the red cell series: all the blood counts were done with automated, calibrated hematology analyzers, in the Earth laboratories the samples returned to (Johnson Space Center, Kennedy Space Center, Star City and the University of Houston). It is the calibration of those analyzers, not that of on-board equipment, and the sentence does not say how often. Only the red cell series, its indices and the platelets, which is what that study measures and calculates; the leukocytes were counted in another study, whose sentence does not name the calibration (`searched_not_found`).
strings.Leído: el actígrafo del inventario del e: Read: the actigraph of the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project) is the Actiwatch Spectrum, a modified commercial device, and its manufacturer (Philips Respironics) sells for the Actiwatch Spectrum a preventive maintenance of “service and recalibration” that includes the calibration of the accelerometer and of the light sensor (Philips service offerings sheet, December 2016). What was read names its calibration, in the manufacturer's service and on request: it does not say that the station unit, which is modified, was recalibrated, or how often. EMMA does not say which actigraph is its own; in the 2023 summary the station carries an Actiwatch Plus, and whether it is the «Actiwatch Spectrum Plus/PRO» of the Philips sheet neither source says.
strings.Leído en el estudio inmunitario de NASA: Read in the NASA immune study with 23 ISS crew members (Crucian et al., 2015), the same one that gives the EDTA tube of the count: the crew was instructed in the blood draw before the mission began, and most of the flight samples were taken as instructed. It is the training of whoever draws blood on the station; it does not say how long it lasted or who gave it, and nothing about the Earth analyzers. Only the leukocytes and their differential: for the red cell series (Kunz et al., 2017) and the biochemistry (Hardy et al., 2025) no training was read (`searched_not_found`).
strings.Leído en un póster sobre un estudio del: Read in a poster about a study of the NASA Ames psychophysiology laboratory, presented at a student symposium of the University of Houston-Clear Lake, on the Astroskin shirt with sensors —the CSA one, which on the ISS is the Bio-Monitor— tested on crews of the HERA analog, on Earth (DeLeon, Cowings and Toscano, 2016): before the mission, on the baseline day, the crew was trained on the equipment and the software of the study («training on hardware/software»), which in that section of the poster is that of the Astroskin, the ergometer and the survey. It is an analog on Earth, not the station, and it is the Astroskin; EMMA does not say that its wearable is that one. It does not say how long the training lasted or who gave it; the CSA Bio-Monitor record and the abstract of NTRS 20190001996 do not speak of training. It reaches what EMMA measures with `wearable` (the heart rate, its two variabilities and the respiratory rate); the pulse oximeter, the temperature sensor and the accelerometer are in EMMA equipment under another name and are not included (`searched_not_found`).
strings.Leído en el informe de evidencia del rie: Read in the evidence report of the renal stone risk (HRP, 2024): the 24-hour urine chemistry with which the risk is assessed is that of the stone risk profile of an Earth laboratory, which is done every year and after the flight, at the medical examination 3 and 30 days after return; on the ISS, blood and urine tests are limited to basic electrolytes and the urine dipstick. The deferred result follows from that: today there is no 24-hour collection analyzed on board. It reaches the eight analytes of the profile (the supersaturation is calculated by the laboratory from them). Qualification: the operations annex of the same report assumes for Mars a urine dipstick for calcium oxalate on board (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído el 2026-10-26 en el resumen técnic: Read on 2026-10-26 in NASA's technical brief on bone loss (OCHMO-MTB-013 Rev D): bone mineral density is monitored on Earth before and after the flight, and no equipment measures it in flight today. Densitometry (DXA) requires the person to be on Earth: it is an analysis on Earth, not of a returned sample. When the result arrives and what it uses up remain unclassified: what was read does not say.
strings.Leído el 2026-10-31 en el protocolo Spac: Read on 2026-10-31 in the Spaceflight Standard Measures protocol (Hardy et al., 2025): body composition by DXA (bone, fat, lean mass) is a medical operations measurement of before and after the flight. Densitometry requires the person to be on Earth, like that of bone density (rule `densitometria-solo-en-tierra`): it is an analysis on Earth, not of a returned sample. When the result arrives and what it uses up remain unclassified: what was read does not say.

Read on 2026-10-31 in the Spaceflight Standard Measures protocol (Hardy et al., 2025): the percentage of correct steps is not given by an instrument on measuring; three reviewers count it afterwards on the video and the median is taken. That is why it is left out of the rule `sin-muestra-periodico`. Where the video is reviewed the sentence does not say: where it is processed remains unclassified, and its consumables too.
strings.`equipment` de este fichero: las nueve p: `equipment` of this file: the nine tests of the Cognition battery with an indicator of their own are run on a laptop (Dev et al. 2024: the crew's; Basner et al. 2015: on the ISS, that of the HRF in the Columbus module) and what is recorded are response times and proportions of correct answers: no sample and no material. On finishing, the result is left encrypted on the laptop itself and, if there is a connection, it is transmitted to a server. Where it is processed and when it arrives is said by the rule of the class (no sample, periodic); of the screen on which it is run, no source read says that it uses anything up, and this rule does not claim it of the screen: it says the test uses no material of its own.
strings.Deducción de EMMA (lo deduce EMMA de la: EMMA's deduction (EMMA deduces it from the measurement class, not from a sentence read): the class “continuous and passive” of this file (`mode`) is what a sensor records while it is worn or running, without anyone making the measurement. It says what intervention the class asks for, not how automated it is on the station today: there the CSA shirt with sensors downlinks its data to Earth for analysis (qualification of `sin-muestra-continuo`), and about the screen, the base or the link that this needs, this rule says nothing.

EMMA's deduction (EMMA deduces it from the measurement class, not from a sentence read): the class “periodic, non-invasive” of this file (`mode`) is a measurement that someone makes or notes down —the crew member with the blood pressure monitor, the dynamometer, the on-screen test or the console; an operator with the ultrasound scanner— and that takes no sample. It does not say who makes it or how long it takes: the former is said by the training where it was read; the latter, by the crew time where it has a source.

EMMA's deduction (EMMA deduces it from the measurement class, not from a sentence read): the classes “periodic, with a sample” and “laboratory” of this file (`mode`) ask for someone to take the sample and for it to be analyzed separately. The rule names the equipment with a sample because the class “laboratory” also carries DXA densitometry, which takes none: for those two, the class does not decide, and they remain unclassified. Where it is processed and when it arrives are said by their rules read; this one does not say whether the analysis could be automated on board: the analyzer demonstrations on the ISS go as qualifications of the blood rule.

EMMA's deduction (EMMA deduces it from the measurement class, not from a sentence read): the class “calculated from other measurements” of this file (`mode`) is a calculation, which is automated when its inputs (`inputs`) are automated. It reaches the two ratios: the cumulative dose, also of this class, is not calculated in EMMA, it arrives recorded from a dosimeter (its `inputs_basis`), and the class does not decide what intervention it asks for: it remains unclassified.
strings.Leído en la ficha del Bio-Monitor de la: Read in the CSA Bio-Monitor record (modified on 26 February 2026): the system of shirt and band with sensors measures the physiological data continuously, and the garments are also worn while sleeping and exercising. It is the station equipment; EMMA does not say that its wearable is that one, and the page does not say how many days per mission it is worn or at what cadence it records. It reaches what EMMA measures with `wearable` (the heart rate, its two variabilities and the respiratory rate); the pulse oximeter, the temperature sensor and the accelerometer are in EMMA equipment under another name and are not included (`searched_not_found`), as with the training.
strings.Leído en el protocolo de medidas estánda: Read in the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 (Hardy et al.): in flight, actigraphy is recorded in 14-day periods 60 days apart, and during those periods it is worn 24/7 except during extravehicular activities or other operational constraints. It is not plainly “continuous”: it is so within each period, and between periods there is no recording; the calendar of the periods is given by the sentences. It is the calendar of that protocol, with its actigraph (an Actiwatch, according to `actigrafo-con-recalibracion-del-fabricante`): EMMA does not say which actigraph is its own.
strings.Leído: el protocolo de medidas estándar: Read: the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 takes blood before, during and after the flight, and sets the flight sessions by the duration of the mission: one in the middle for short ones (up to 105 days); in the first month, in the middle and in the last month for those of 105 to 240 days; and one more for those over 240 (Hardy et al., 2025). The ISS nutrition experiment took blood and urine five times in flight (Smith et al., 2012). The sentences give the calendar of the blood draw, not that of each analyte: they name blood, not sodium or CA-125, and none says that those protocols measure EMMA's tumor markers. EMMA applies it to what it measures in serum because the possible frequency of a serum analyte is that of the blood draw that gives it, and says so here: the cadence is that of those two protocols, not one of EMMA's. The blood count is not included: its studies give their own calendar (`leucocitos-en-tres-sesiones-de-vuelo`, `serie-roja-en-tres-sesiones-de-vuelo`).
strings.Leído en el estudio inmunitario de NASA: Read in the NASA immune study with 23 ISS crew members (Crucian et al., 2015), the same one that gives the EDTA tube of the count: blood was taken in flight at three points —around day 14, between months 2 and 4 and around 6 months— always shortly before a visiting vehicle undocked, to return it to Earth. It is the calendar of that study, tied to the returns: the possible frequency was that of the vehicles that returned.
strings.Leído en el estudio de NASA sobre el hem: Read in the NASA study on the blood count of 31 ISS crew members (Kunz et al., 2017), the same one that gives the EDTA tube of the red cell series: in flight, blood was taken in the first two weeks, between months 2 and 4 and around 6 months, just before return, coinciding with crew returns so that it reached the laboratory in under 48 h. It is the calendar of that study, tied to the returns.
strings.Leído en el estudio de NASA sobre virus: Read in the NASA study on latent viruses in long ISS missions (Mehta et al., 2017), the same one that gives the filter paper and the Salivettes: saliva was taken in seven sessions, three of them in flight (around day 14, between days 60 and 120 and around day 180), with four samples per session for the viruses and, for diurnal cortisol, five a day on each sampling day. It is the calendar of that study; in the 2025 standard measures protocol the saliva for virology is also taken before, during and after the flight (Hardy et al., table 2), with the flight sessions of `sangre-del-protocolo-en-sesiones-de-vuelo`.
strings.Leído: el experimento de nutrición de la: Read: the ISS nutrition experiment took blood and urine five times in flight to analyze them after return (Smith et al., 2012). The sentence speaks of the urine sample, not of the marker: it reaches the 24 h volume and the NTX, which is measured in laboratory urine, like the rule of the bags. Qualifications: in the 2025 standard measures protocol there is no urine collection in flight, and in the latent virus study the 24 h pool was collected only before and after the flight (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído en el protocolo de medidas estánda: Read in the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 (Hardy et al.): the cognitive battery (CTB) is run before, during and after the flight (table 2, row «Cognitive test battery»: «Pre/In/Post»; and the sentence about the 25 astronauts, whose changes were seen «during flight»), one of its ten tests is the psychomotor vigilance one, and the flight sessions are those of the protocol (in the middle for short missions; first month, middle and last month for those of 105 to 240 days; one more for long ones). It is the calendar of the CTB, which carries the PVT inside a battery of ten tests; EMMA runs the 3-minute PVT-B on its own (`crew_time_basis`), and the sentence does not say that it is the same version.
strings.Leído en el informe de evidencia del rie: Read in the evidence report of the renal stone risk (HRP, 2024), the same one that gives where the profile is processed: the assessment is done every year and after the flight, at the medical examination 3 and 30 days after return. The NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025 confirms it for itself: there is no urine collection in flight, and its table 2 gives the «Renal stone profile» as «Pre/Post». That is why here it is an Earth calendar: with no 24-hour collection in flight, there is nothing to store on board. Qualifications: another experiment did collect urine in flight and does not say which analytes it measured (see discrepancies), and that is what supports the five collections of `orina-de-vuelo-en-cinco-tomas`; and the operations annex for Mars assumes a urine dipstick for calcium oxalate on board, which is not this profile (see `perfil-litiasico-en-tierra`).
strings.Leído en el resumen técnico de NASA sobr: Read in NASA's technical brief on bone loss (OCHMO-MTB-013 Rev D), the same one that gives where it is processed: bone mineral density is monitored on Earth before and after the flight, and no equipment measures it in flight today. With no measurement in flight, there is nothing to store on board. The sentence does not say how often it is repeated on Earth.
strings.Leído: en el protocolo de medidas estánd: Read: in the NASA standard measures protocol described in 2025, the flight samples, after centrifuging, go to the ISS freezer at -96 °C until they return to Earth (Hardy et al., 2025); and “today” the blood taken on the ISS is frozen and returned to be analyzed after the mission (Brawley et al., 2025). The sentences speak of the sample, not of each analyte: they reach what EMMA measures in serum, like the rule of the tubes. The blood count is not included: its studies returned the blood at ambient temperature (`leucocitos-devueltos-a-temperatura-ambiente`, `serie-roja-en-bolsas-a-temperatura-ambiente`). How much room it takes in the freezer no sentence says.
strings.Leído en el estudio inmunitario de NASA: Read in the NASA immune study with 23 ISS crew members (Crucian et al., 2015): the flight blood was returned to Earth at once, at ambient temperature, in under 48 h, because there was no immunology or hematology analytical equipment on board. The sample waits at ambient temperature for as long as the vehicle takes; the sentence does not say where or in what it was stored meanwhile.
strings.Leído en el estudio de NASA sobre el hem: Read in the NASA study on the blood count of 31 ISS crew members (Kunz et al., 2017): the flight blood was stored in custom blood bags and passed to the return vehicle, at ambient temperature, to be analyzed on Earth in under 48 h. Qualification: the same study says that blood at ambient temperature returned from space is rare (see discrepancies): it is what that study did, not ordinary use.
strings.Leído en el estudio de NASA sobre virus: Read in the NASA study on latent viruses in long ISS missions (Mehta et al., 2017), the same one that gives the Salivettes: the saliva samples were stored at ambient temperature for about two weeks until returning to Earth. Qualification: in the 2025 standard measures protocol the saliva for virology is stored frozen until processing, without saying where (see discrepancies).
strings.Leído en el mismo estudio (Mehta et al.,: Read in the same study (Mehta et al., 2017), the one that gives the filter paper: the saliva for diurnal cortisol was left to air-dry on the paper and stored at ambient temperature until the return to Earth.
strings.Los dos cocientes se calculan de los ana: The two ratios are calculated from the analytes of the same report (`reports/labs.py`; their `inputs` in this file): they add no sample to store and no schedule of their own; they are available when their inputs are. The storage and the frequency of their inputs are not inherited (only where they are processed and when they arrive, `INHERITED_DIMENSIONS`). The cumulative dose is left out, as in `calculo-sin-equipo-propio`: it arrives recorded; it is not calculated in EMMA.
strings.Si el glucómetro se calibra y qué formac: Whether the glucose meter is calibrated and what training its user has. Read in full: the CDC page «Monitoring Your Blood Sugar» and the MedlinePlus page «Blood sugar test»: neither names calibration or a control solution. The CDC says that most glucose meters work the same way and that the health care team should show how to use it («There are different kinds of meters, but most of them work the same way. Ask your health care team to show you how they work.»), without saying what training or how long it lasts, and it speaks of people with diabetes on Earth. Whether there is a glucose meter on board the ISS and who is trained to use it: no source that says so has been read.
strings.Si el test casero de ovulación se calibr: Whether the home ovulation test is calibrated and what training its user has. Reread: the MedlinePlus page «Ovulation home test» (reviewed on 22 May 2025) that what was read about the measurement already cites: the first paragraph, «How the Test is Performed», «How to Prepare for the Test», «How the Test will Feel» and «Normal Results». It names no calibration or control solution; about how it is used it only says that the kit booklet explains how to read the result («The booklet that is included in the kit will tell you how to read the results.»), without saying what training or how long it lasts, and it speaks of people on Earth. The same page says the result is seen on the strip itself («The test stick will turn a certain color or display a positive sign if a surge is detected.»): there is no separate analysis, and that is why the automation capability is not deduced from the class “periodic, with a sample” either (like the glucose meter). No manufacturer's documentation was read. Whether there are ovulation tests on board the ISS: no source that says so has been read.
strings.Dónde y con qué se mide en vuelo la dens: Where and with what urine specific gravity is measured in flight. Searched on 2026-10-21 in NTRS («urine specific gravity flight»: only studies on Earth —bed rest, acceleration and lower body negative pressure— and one compared with Skylab data; «urine specific gravity spaceflight»: one study of EVA training in a pool), in the abstract of NTRS 20140013382 (laboratory analysis for exploration missions: it speaks of what will be needed, not of what is on the ISS today), in the full text of Hardy et al. 2025 («specific gravity» and «refractometer» do not appear) and on the web for the ISS medical kit (CHeCS) and its urine dipsticks, and for the Biochemical Profile experiment. Searched again on 2026-10-22: the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project, slide 21) lists as urine consumables the collection device, the containment bag, the syringes and a pH kit, nothing for specific gravity; and the web search for test strips or a refractometer in the ISS medical kit returned only studies on Earth. No sentence says where or with what it is measured.
strings.Si gastan material los sensores que se l: Whether the sensors that are worn use up material. Read: the CSA Bio-Monitor record (shirt and band with metal sensors against the skin and a battery that plugs into a base; it names no consumables, single-use electrodes, gel or replacement garments), the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project: the Actiwatch Spectrum record —watch, base, cable and software— names no consumables; the electrodes of the supply kit are named only by the Holter record, which is not the equipment of any EMMA indicator) and the abstract of NTRS 20190001996 (Astroskin in HERA: that the system uses few consumables is what NASA asks of a future system, not what Astroskin is said to use). The equipment records of the ISS Research Explorer (Bio-Monitor, Actiwatch Spectrum) load in the browser and the reading tool does not see them; its downloadable listing (All_Facilities_Report.xlsx) gives name, responsible parties, expeditions and category, not the description. That a record names no consumables does not say that none are used up.
strings.Qué gasta la toma de la presión arterial: What taking blood pressure in flight uses up. The ISS Research Explorer listing names a continuous blood pressure device of the HRF (Continuous Blood Pressure Device, expeditions 13 to 43/44), whose record could not be read (it loads in the browser); the CSA Bio-Monitor record says it measures blood pressure, not how or with what material; the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project) lists no blood pressure monitor. No sentence says what it uses up.
strings.Qué gasta la medida de masa en micrograv: What the mass measurement in microgravity uses up. The 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project, slide 13) describes the SLAMMD —two springs push the crew member mounted on an arm and the acceleration gives the mass— without naming consumables; the ISS Research Explorer record could not be read (it loads in the browser). That it does not name them does not say that it uses none.
strings.Qué gasta la prueba de esfuerzo con anal: What the exercise test with gas analyzer (CEVIS cycle ergometer and Portable PFS) uses up. Read: the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical equipment (ISS Medical Project, slide 11: the Pulmonary Function System, with accessories for rebreathing and a mixing bag, without naming consumables), the Portable PFS page of its manufacturer, Danish Aerospace Company (it takes the gas from NASA's Gas Delivery System; it does not say how much a test uses or name mouthpieces, nose clips or filters), ESA's page on the PFS (27 October 2005: nothing on consumables) and the abstract of the peak VO2 study on the ISS (Moore et al., NTRS 20140003748: it does not describe the equipment). The full article of that study (J Appl Physiol) answered 403, and the ISS Research Explorer records (CEVIS, PFS, Portable PFS) load in the browser. No sentence says that the test uses up mouthpieces, filters or gas.
strings.Qué gasta el dinamómetro de mano. El lis: What the hand dynamometer uses up. The ISS Research Explorer listing names a hand grip and pinch dynamometer (Hand Grip Dynamometer-Pinch Force Dynamometer, by Kayser Italia, expeditions 7, 8, 11 and 16), whose record could not be read (it loads in the browser); the web search for that name returned no record of the equipment, and the 2016 inventory (ISS Medical Project) does not list it. No sentence says what it uses up.
strings.Dónde se calcula la dosis acumulada que: Where the cumulative dose that arrives recorded is calculated. Read: the page of NASA's Space Radiation Analysis Group (srag.jsc.nasa.gov, «How do we protect the astronauts from space radiation?», updated on 24 September 2025): on the ISS there are two paths. Passive dosimetry gives the mission dose only on return; since 2020, the Crew Active Dosimeters measure and record each crew member's dose during the mission, send it by Bluetooth to the on-board laptops to downlink it to the SRAG and show the total mission dose on their screen. EMMA does not say which of the two its dose arrives from (`POST /api/observations`, from a dosimeter): choosing one would be classifying by eye, and it remains unclassified.
strings.Masa, tamaño, potencia y calibración del: Mass, size, power and calibration of the ultrasound scanner. Read in full: the 2016 inventory of the ISS medical research equipment (ISS Medical Project) and the 2023 summary of the human research facilities (NASA HRP, NTRS 20230009091): of the Ultrasound 2 they give the model (a modified GE Vivid q), the probes and the accessories, and that it plugs into the HRF rack to draw power; of the rack, that each payload can use up to 500 W and all together up to 2000 W. That is a ceiling of the rack, not what the scanner draws, and it is not written as its power. The only mass and the only size in the 2023 document are those of the accessory kit of the electroretinograph, which is not the equipment of any EMMA indicator. The manufacturer's data sheet for the Vivid q was searched for on the web: only those of its successor (Vivid iq) turned up, which is a different device. From the 2019 jugular study (Marshall-Goebel et al.) the only calibration is that of a manometer that was zeroed before each venous pressure measurement, which is not a measurement of EMMA.
strings.Quién guía la toma de las demás ecografí: Who guides the acquisition of the other ultrasound scans and what training the person doing it has. The 2019 jugular study took only the left one. The abstract of a 2004 NASA paper on remote ultrasound on the ISS (NTRS 20110011352, Sargsyan et al.) says that astronaut training usually ensures they work on their own and that there have been sessions guided in real time, without naming the optic nerve sheath or the bladder. The two inventories (2016 and 2023) do not speak of training.
strings.Masa, tamaño y potencia del SLAMMD y for: Mass, size and power of the SLAMMD and training of whoever operates it. Its records in the 2016 inventory and in the 2023 summary give its principle (two springs, a known force and the acceleration it produces) and its accuracy, not its mass, size, power draw or training; the daily report of 29 October 2019 tells of its calibration and says nothing of that either.
strings.Masa, tamaño y potencia del analizador d: Mass, size and power of the gas analyzer of the exercise test and training of whoever operates it. The 2016 inventory describes the PFS (modules, measurements and an electronics unit that takes up a rack drawer) and the 2023 summary the cylinders of the gas system (their capacity, not the size of the analyzer); neither gives mass, size or power draw of the analyzer, or training.
strings.Masa, tamaño, batería y calibración del: Mass, size, battery and calibration of the actigraph. The 2016 inventory names the Actiwatch Spectrum (watch, base, cable and software) and the 2023 summary the Actiwatch Plus (water-resistant, on the wrist, with a three-axis accelerometer and a light sensor): neither gives mass, size, battery or calibration. EMMA does not say which actigraph is its own. The above is what those two documents gave on 2026-10-23. The calibration, which they did not give, turned up later in another source, the service sheet of the Actiwatch Spectrum's manufacturer (read on 2026-10-26; rule `actigrafo-con-recalibracion-del-fabricante`), and this note no longer counts it as not found: the rest remains with no source, mass, size and battery.
strings.Masa, tamaño, potencia, calibración y fo: Mass, size, power, calibration and training of the blood pressure monitor and of the hand dynamometer. The 2023 facilities summary lists neither a blood pressure monitor nor a dynamometer among its equipment; the 2019 jugular study names the ambulatory blood pressure monitor that was used on the ISS (Tonoport V, by GE) without giving any of that. The ISS Research Explorer records still cannot be read with the tool (fifteenth round).
strings.Si se calibran los sensores que se lleva: Whether the sensors that are worn are calibrated. Read: the CSA Bio-Monitor record (modified on 26 February 2026: shirt, band, metal sensors against the skin, battery and base; it does not speak of calibration), the abstract of NTRS 20190001996 and the poster of NTRS 20190000238 (the Astroskin in the HERA analog: data quality, comfort and Bluetooth, nothing on calibration). The web search («Bio-Monitor Astroskin ISS astronaut training calibration CSA») returned only pages of the manufacturer (Hexoskin) and press pages about its use on the ISS, none with its calibration. For EMMA's pulse oximeter, temperature sensor and accelerometer no station equipment with that name was read. That a record does not speak of calibration does not say that it needs none.
strings.Qué formación lleva quien usa el pulsiox: What training the user of the pulse oximeter, the temperature sensor, the accelerometer and the actigraph has. The poster of the HERA analog (NTRS 20190000238) tells of the training on the Astroskin, which carries a band with a saturation sensor and measures skin temperature and activity, but EMMA names that equipment separately and does not say that it is that of the shirt; the CSA Bio-Monitor record does not speak of training; for the actigraph, neither does the Actiwatch Spectrum record in the 2016 ISS inventory (watch, base, cable and software) nor the service sheet of its manufacturer (Philips).
strings.Qué formación lleva quien maneja el dosí: What training whoever operates the ship dosimeter has. Berger et al. 2017 (the DOSTELs of DOSIS 3D) tells of their mounting under the EPM rack of Columbus, the data downlink through that rack every four weeks and thanks the astronauts who worked on the experiment, without speaking of their training; the SRAG page (updated on 24 September 2025) describes the RAD, the REMs, the HERA and the Crew Active Dosimeters without speaking of training.
strings.Calibración y formación del dosímetro de: Calibration and training for the dosimeter the cumulative dose arrives from. The SRAG page (updated on 24 September 2025) says of the Crew Active Dosimeters that they go from the electrical changes to an absorbed dose with a relationship obtained in calibrations on Earth, and of passive dosimetry it does not say how it is calibrated. EMMA does not say which of the two its dose arrives from (for the same reason where it is processed was left unclassified, on 2026-10-22), and choosing one would be classifying by eye. About training, the page says nothing.
strings.Si se calibran los analizadores de la sa: Whether the blood, urine and saliva analyzers are calibrated, except that of the red cell series blood count. Reread: Crucian et al. 2015 (the leukocyte count was done with «a standard clinical hematology analyzer», without naming its calibration), Hardy et al. 2025 (full text in Europe PMC: «calibrat» does not appear), Mehta et al. 2017 (the saliva and urine of the latent viruses and the cortisol: not there either) and the PDF of NTRS 20130000839 (Smith et al., nutritional status: not there either). For the 24 h urine volume, the abstract of NTRS 20090007818 names the on-orbit calibration of the UMS that flew on the shuttles (slow), not that of the lithium method with which it is calculated on Earth today. That the text does not name the calibration does not say that the analyzer is not calibrated.
strings.Qué formación lleva quien toma la sangre: What training whoever takes the blood, the urine and the saliva has, except the blood draw of the leukocyte study. Reread: Kunz et al. 2017 (a photo of an astronaut doing a blood draw on the ISS, without saying her training), Hardy et al. 2025 (it names crew training only as something to take into account when taking the protocol to private missions), Mehta et al. 2017 and the PDF of NTRS 20130000839: none says what training whoever takes the sample has. The NTRS abstracts on urine collection (20090013860, 20090007818 and 20110008547) tell what the crew member does, not their training.
strings.Con qué frecuencia se puede medir con el: How often it is possible to measure with the pulse oximeter, the temperature sensor and the accelerometer. The CSA Bio-Monitor record says the shirt with sensors measures continuously, but EMMA names those three pieces of equipment separately and does not say that they are those of the shirt (as with the training, on 2026-10-26); the 2025 standard measures protocol (Hardy et al., table 1, shared medical operations measures) lists temperature, saturation and respiratory rate in the periodic in-flight health status («Periodic Health Status», «In»), with no cadence. No sentence gives the frequency of that equipment.
strings.Cuánto ocupan los datos de los sensores: How much room the data of the sensors that are worn and of the actigraph take. The CSA Bio-Monitor record says the system records the data («records vital sign data») and that the battery plugs into a base that downlinks them to Earth, with no volume figure; the 2025 standard measures protocol (Hardy et al.) describes the recording periods of actigraphy and that the protocol's data are stored in NASA's life sciences archive («Data from these crewmembers are stored in the Standard Measures repository within the NASA Life Sciences Data Archives»), without the volume of either. No sentence read gives a data volume, and with no figure the storage of a datum remains unclassified.
strings.Cada cuánto se mide la masa corporal en: How often body mass is measured in flight. The 2025 standard measures protocol (Hardy et al., table 1, shared medical operations measures) says «Body mass is measured periodically in flight using the Russian Mass Measurement Device»: periodic, with no cadence, and with the Russian device, not the SLAMMD whose calibration was read. With no cadence there is no calendar to copy.
strings.Cada cuánto se toman en vuelo la presión: How often blood pressure and the exercise test are taken in flight. The 2025 standard measures protocol (Hardy et al., table 1, shared medical operations measures) lists blood pressure and pulse in the periodic in-flight health status («Periodic Health Status», «In») and the cycle ergometer exercise test as «Pre/In/Post», neither with a cadence; the flight sessions of the protocol (first month, middle, last month) are those of its own measures, not those of medical operations. No sentence gives the cadence.
strings.Cómo se guarda a bordo la orina de vuelo: How flight urine is stored on board. Mehta et al. 2017 says the aliquot of the 24 h pool was frozen until return («frozen until return to Earth»), but in that study the pool was collected before and after the flight, and the volume of each flight void is calculated from the lithium of its syringe sample, about whose preservation on board it says nothing; the abstract of NTRS 20090013860 only says «for later ground analysis»; in the 2025 standard measures protocol there is no urine in flight. For the NTX (Smith et al., 2012, one-page abstract) it is not read how the urine was stored. No sentence says how it waits on board.
strings.Cada cuánto se mide y cómo se guarda la: How often urine specific gravity is measured and how it is stored in flight. The 2025 standard measures protocol (Hardy et al.) does not name specific gravity (already searched on 2026-10-21) and its table 1 lists «Urine analysis» among the laboratory tests of medical operations only before and after the flight («Pre/Post»), without saying what it includes; the renal stone risk report (HRP, 2024, page 24) says that on the ISS there is a urine dipstick («urine dipstick testing») without giving a cadence. No sentence gives the calendar or says what is stored.
